This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/lint`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **15** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

- `content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx`  _(via relationshipField (literal, a string literal in masterDetailDetailEntry))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/ui.json`, `packages/spec/dropped-refinements.baseline.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/ui.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **6** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e18fea6dcdf6af5619cae05eb37c38417230d83b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e7e00637e6f3b0e5f5990cb12a9b923e57e10bdc` — the merge of head `bfb26d52e9a14b9f3808510e00aa6400f5c7f9fd` into base `e18fea6dcdf6af5619cae05eb37c38417230d83b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e7e00637e6f3b0e5f5990cb12a9b923e57e10bdc && git checkout e7e00637e6f3b0e5f5990cb12a9b923e57e10bdc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e18fea6dcdf6af5619cae05eb37c38417230d83b bfb26d52e9a14b9f3808510e00aa6400f5c7f9fd && git checkout -B drift-repro e18fea6dcdf6af5619cae05eb37c38417230d83b && git merge --no-ff bfb26d52e9a14b9f3808510e00aa6400f5c7f9fd

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e18fea6dcdf6af5619cae05eb37c38417230d83b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e18fea6dcdf6af5619cae05eb37c38417230d83b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bfb26d52e9a14b9f3808510e00aa6400f5c7f9fd`
Local-runs: none

Inputs, and nothing else: card #20928 (body, triage 5919655566, claim 5934221277, dev report 5936596153), PR #21215 (body, its 15-file list, the net diff of the branch at the head against `origin/main`, merge-base `0d421041d`), and the head's check-runs. Read-only reads of `origin/main` and of the pinned objectui at `31971ff1e28f` (the `.objectui-sha` on `origin/main` and on the merge-base) were taken to judge the claims; nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `ComponentPropsMap['object-master-detail-form'].details` element goes from `z.unknown()` to a strict entry of twelve keys. RIGHT. objectui `packages/plugin-form/src/MasterDetailForm.tsx` at `31971ff1e28f` declares `MasterDetailDetailConfig` with exactly these twelve members (lines 64 to 93), each with a live `d.X` read; the other member reads in the file (`detail.saving`, `detail.add`, `d.input`) are an i18n key pair and a batch-input map, not config keys. `inlineMode` as `grid | form` equals the renderer's `InlineMode` (`deriveMasterDetail.ts:423`). `title` and `addLabel` as plain strings match the renderer (a React child at `:755`, a button label at `:865`) and the subforms entry. `childObject` required matches the renderer's declined branch (`:986`).
2. The keys shared with the form view's `subforms[]` entry take that entry's types and alias table. RIGHT, byte-equal against `view.zod.ts` on `origin/main`: the ten-alias table and the types of `childObject`, `relationshipField`, `columns`, `amountField`, `totalField`, `title`, `addLabel`, `minRows`, `maxRows`. The three added keys (`formFields`, `inlineMode`, `sortField`) are renderer-read. No alias collides with a declared key.
3. `columns` references `InlineGridColumnSchema` by object identity, not a copy. RIGHT, and pinned by the `toBe` case. Rulings B (#19629) and 乙 (#19910) reach this carrier through the column schema's own refinement; no second scale rule was written.
4. Accept-set effect: a narrowing on a published export (`ObjectMasterDetailFormPropsSchema`, `ui` namespace, listed in `api-surface/ui.json`). Refused now: an entry without `childObject`, an unknown entry key, a bare-string column, a `field`-keyed column, an unknown column key, `scale` on a column declaring `type: 'currency'`. The named producer's entry `{ title, childObject, addLabel }` parses unchanged. A bare-string column gets zod's own `expected object, received string` (no alias is possible for a string); the changeset's FROM → TO table and the D3 `replacement` text carry that prescription. RIGHT.
5. Public surface: one additive type export, `ObjectMasterDetailFormPropsParsed` (`api-surface/ui.json` and `export-origins/ui.json` regenerated; the isomorphism pin count 779 → 778 by the pin file's own prescribed route). RIGHT: input and infer differ because the column's `readonlyWhen` / `requiredWhen` bare-string arm transforms to an envelope.
6. `stack.zod.ts`: the page-component traversal is extracted into `forEachPageComponent`. RIGHT: the regions, slots and nested-array walk and its path spellings are byte-identical to the former `collectInlinePageActions` body, and the inline-action collector now reuses it.
7. The new precondition inside `judge` (a column is judged only when `InlineGridColumnSchema.safeParse(column)` succeeds without the type). RIGHT on all three carriers. `validateCrossReferences` receives the parsed `data`, so on the two parsed carriers the column is parse output, and `EvaluatedExpressionInputSchema` is a union whose envelope arm accepts its own output, so the re-parse is stable and the guard is a no-op there. On the raw page carrier it stops a column's own defects from being reported as currency findings (ablation A3 printed exactly that misattribution). Reach is unchanged: a declared `type` is skipped, an undeclared child object or field is skipped.
8. Page-carrier reach: `config.pages` only, every region, slot and nested container array, the same reach the inline-action cross-reference check already has. RIGHT and consistent.
9. `validate-field-consumers.ts`: `CHILD_COLLECTION_KEYS` gains `details`. RIGHT. The walk treats every array element under a `details` key as a child entry. The only other `details` arrays in stack metadata are the page slot map's (components, which carry none of an entry's keys at their own level, pinned by the control case) and API error payloads the scan never walks. `totalField` stays parent-scoped through the general walk and is pinned so.
10. ADR-0087: D3 entry `ui-object-master-detail-form-details-closed` plus a step-18 rationale fragment at order 56 (unique among the fragments; the `(#20928)` citation inside a rationale text follows ten sibling fragments that cite the same way). No D2 conversion. RIGHT: `PageComponentSchema.properties` is `z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())`, and outside spec and lint tests the only `ComponentPropsMap` consumer is the dogfood expression-conformance ledger, so nothing on a save or load door parses component props and nothing at rest is refused.
11. `dropped-refinements.baseline.json` gains one site, `details.element.columns.element`, the exact analogue of `ui/FormView`'s `subforms.element.columns.element`; the hand-edited ledger grows because `build-schemas` refuses an undeclared site. RIGHT.
12. Generated artefacts (`references/ui/component.mdx`, the strictness ledger counts with one more strict site in `component.zod.ts`) and the `layout-dsl.mdx` producer rewrite (the renderer's `hydrateColumns` cannot draw a string column). RIGHT.
13. Governed surfaces: none in the file list; the record is owed by the `Clause-②: yes` and `packages/spec/src/**` limbs, not by tier. Head repo equals base repo; 805 changed lines.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/20928-master-detail-details-closed.md`: `@objectstack/spec: minor`, `@objectstack/lint: patch`; `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`; a BREAKING banner; exactly one adr-0087 disposition marker, `registered ui-object-master-detail-form-details-closed`, in the comment form the gate reads; a FROM → TO table with the one-line fix; the census on `ebdb6f2aca`. RIGHT, each clause:
- `yes` takes at least `minor`: yes. `(narrowing)` is BREAKING and carries its migration: yes. `minor` for a breaking accept-set narrowing is the repo's launch-window convention (fourteen sibling changesets on `main` say so; `check-changeset-no-major` refuses `major`).
- The additive `ObjectMasterDetailFormPropsParsed` export is covered by `minor`.
- `@objectstack/lint: patch`: a false-positive fix in `field-no-consumers`, no export or option change.
- No tombstone owed: nothing declared was removed, the carrier was `z.unknown()`; `retiredKey()` does not apply.
- Declaration consistency: claim 5934221277 declares `Clause-②: yes`, the PR body repeats it verbatim, the changeset adds the `(narrowing)` arm where the registration gate reads it. One arm at most, consistent. `skip-changeset` correctly not applied (spec and lint publish). `Check Changeset` on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev `open_questions`: none. Each deviation and out-of-scope finding in report 5936596153:
- D1 Files beyond the claim's surface (`layout-dsl.mdx`, `type-alias-convention.pin.test.ts`, `dropped-refinements.baseline.json`): ANSWERED, forced by the diff (ablation A5 red, the Iso pin route, the build-schemas refusal); no scope expansion. Claim-listed files left untouched (`conversions/registry.ts`, the showcase page): ANSWERED, correct, no D2 is owed and the showcase entry is inside the twelve keys.
- D2 `forEachPageComponent` extraction: ANSWERED, verified unchanged (①6).
- D3 Entry built by a factory inside the parent's lazy body rather than a standalone `lazySchema`: ANSWERED, acceptable; the alias-integrity walk reaches it, and the subforms entry is built the same way.
- D4 PR body `Clause-②: yes` with no arm while the changeset carries `(narrowing)`: ANSWERED in ②.
- D5 Pin citation repointed to `31971ff1e28f`: ANSWERED; it equals `.objectui-sha` on `origin/main` and on the merge-base, and every cited line resolves there.
- D6 `origin/main` moved after the merge (`e18fea6d`; its only spec file is `data/filter.zod.ts`, untouched here): ANSWERED; the queue rebuilds on current `main`.
- D7 Commit trailers in the model-free pair: ANSWERED, correct per AGENTS.md.
- F1 The objectui coordination child (the `MasterDetailForm` mirror, and `apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` row `object-master-detail-form.details`, whose prose and probes state the spec row is `z.array(z.unknown())`): ESCALATED to the seat as its owed act; the triage and the claim both assign that filing to the seat, not to this PR. Not a landing blocker here: this is a narrowing, not a removal; at the pin the only non-test importer takes the schema by reference through `stripImportedDefaults`, whose walker handles lazy, object, array, union and pipe nodes and falls through on the rest; and `Console Pin Gate` builds the pinned console, it does not run objectui's suites. Those suites against this spec stay NOT MEASURED, as the dev states.
- F2 `field-no-consumers` still reads a detail entry's `sortField` and `formFields` in the parent's context (`CHILD_ENTRY_FIELD_KEYS` is `amountField` and `relationshipField` only): ESCALATED. Two child-field keys credited against the wrong object is a real gap on this carrier, reach unmeasured; it belongs on #21091 (the named family carrier, same file) as a comment, not only in this PR's acceptance notes.
- F3 Two enforcement tiers (advisory component-props findings for the entry and column half, a hard `STACK_CROSS_REFERENCE_INVALID` for the identity-only half; the save door does not parse props): ANSWERED; declared in the changeset, the D3 entry and the acceptance notes, so the claim is as narrow as the enforcement (Prime Directive #10).

No check-run on the head has failed. A running gate is not a pass: landing waits for the four to conclude green (the `Test Core` aggregate context among them).
